title: Priority tokenflow stabilizer for multi-variant throughput collapse
creator: Ana Cortez
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported intermittent first-token-time (TTFT) spikes and sustained tokens/sec throughput collapse during short-session workloads. The symptom pattern: 5-15s TTFT spikes on short prompts (<64 tokens) and sustained throughput degradation (down to 30-40% of baseline) for 1-6 minute windows. Incidents started after onboarding staged 12B quantized variants and a new kernel-selection heuristic for mixed-precision paths. Affected models: rwd-12b-int8, rwd-7b-q4f, and a few community variants used by customers. This ticket coordinates immediate mitigations, root cause verification, and an engineered stabilization before the next runtime release.
acceptance_criteria: TTFT P95 for short-session traffic returns to baseline within one release window and remains stable below 2s on monitored tenants
Tokens/sec (aggregate) recovers to >= 90% of pre-regression baseline during targeted traffic scenarios
Automated canary verifies no regression on mixed quantized/mixed-precision models in Hosted and Dedicated clusters
Rollout plan documented with clear abort criteria and postmortem scheduled

2025-11-04 11:40 - Investigated kernel-selection logs and KV cache eviction traces; found correlated prefetch storms originating from scheduler heuristics when heterogenous model variants co-located
2025-11-05 02:22 - Deployed temporary rate limiter for short-context multiplex queues to reduce token fanout; observed partial recovery for Dedicated pools
2025-11-05 18:10 - Reverted heuristic change in selector (rollback commit: github.com/redwood/inference/commit/ff3b9e) on a small canary cluster; measured TTFT P95 improvement of ~45% in canary

telemetry: New dashboards added: 'Priority Tokenflow — Short Session TTFT', 'KV Prefetch Rate vs Eviction', 'Kernel Selector Decision Heatmap'. Alerts: TTFT P95 > 2.5s for >5m triggers P0 on-call. Synthetic canaries run every 5m across Hosted/Dedicated/Private clusters. Traces correlated by request-id to identify cross-tenant scheduling conflicts.
root_cause_summary: A regression in the kernel-selection heuristic introduced when adding optimized kernels for int8 paths. Under mixed-variant load patterns (small prompts hitting int8 variants interleaved with long-context quantized models), the scheduler favored an optimized kernel that held KV-cache reservations longer than expected. That interacted poorly with our continuous batching layer, causing batch formation stalls and excessive KV-prefetch which triggered thrashing on workers that serve multiple tenants. The net effect: initial-token delays and reduced token emission rate until the KV cache and prefetch backpressure cleared.
rollback_plan: If canary rollback fails or TTFT does not improve by 30% within 60 minutes of deployment, revert selector to previous stable commit (github.com/redwood/inference/commit/7a1d2c) and re-enable conservative kernel-path gating. Abort criteria: sustained TTFT P95 increase on canary > 20% or tokens/sec below 80% baseline after 45 minutes. Communication: notify SRE and impacted customers in #escalations and runbook update 'rbw/priority-tokenflow-stabilizer'.
followups: Postmortem with timeline and RCA to be published within 72 hours
Refactor kernel-selection heuristic to include per-worker KV-reservation budget and backpressure signals
Add integration test that simulates mixed-variant short/long prompt traffic at scale
Optimize KV-prefetch to be priority-aware (short-session requests get prefetched first, with stricter timeouts)
Evaluate dedicated-tenant isolation knobs to avoid cross-tenant eviction thrash in Dedicated mode
